chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said, 'Your wife, the Shaybaniyya, is a Kharijite who insults Ali (peace be upon him). If it pleases you that I let you hear it from her, I will let you hear it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So when tomorrow comes, at the time you intend to go out as you usually do, return and hide by the side of the house.' He said, 'So when it was the next day, he hid by the side of the house. The man came and spoke to her, and that (insulting Ali) became clear from her. So he freed her way (divorced her), and although he used to like her.'

key_terms.الشَّيْبَانِيَّةَ: The Shaybaniyya, a female member of the Shayban tribe, often used to denote a specific woman in this context.
key_terms.جَانِبِ الدَّارِ: The side of the house, the location for hiding/listening.
key_terms.خَارِجِيَّةٌ: Kharijite, a member of the Kharijite sect known for their theological views.
key_terms.فَخَلَّى سَبِيلَهَا: He freed her way, a phrase indicating divorce (talaq).

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn verify his wife's religious sect before divorcing her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of 'al-walāʾ wa-l-barāʾ' (loyalty and disloyalty) in marital jurisprudence, where Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) prioritized doctrinal fidelity over personal affection. The verification process highlights the Kharijite tendency to curse the Ahl al-Bayt as a definitive marker of their sect, a criterion used to validate the dissolution of the marriage despite the Imam's emotional attachment to his wife.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

A man came over to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> so he said, ‘Your<sup>asws</sup> wife, the Shaybaniyya foreigner tends to insult Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so if you<sup>asws</sup> want to secretly hear that from her, I can make you<sup>asws</sup> hear it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. He said, ‘So when it is the morning when you<sup>asws</sup> want to come out just as you normally tend to come out, so stand by the side of the house’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So when it was the morning, he<sup>asws</sup> stood by the side of the house, so the man came over and spoke to her, and that (insulting Ali<sup>asws</sup>) was manifested from her. So he<sup>asws</sup> freed her way (divorced her), and (although) he<sup>asws</sup> used to like her’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Once a man came to Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said, “Your wife from al-Shayban people is of Kharijiy sect who vilify Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. If you like I can manage for you to hear what she says.” He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, I agree.’ He (man) said, ‘Tomorrow as you come out of your home as you normally do, wait on the side of the house.’ Next day he (the Imam) waited on the side of the house and the man came. He spoke to her and it (vilification) became clear from her. He (the Imam) divorced her although he liked her quite well.’”
